calculation.activity: LIQUID-only equilibria; reference pure liquid at T
calculation.field_map: own pycalphad equilibrium grid, dx 0.01 (ends 1e-5), dT 10 K; fields = connected cells with equal labelled assemblage
calculation.formation: single-phase equilibrium at 298.15 K; HM relative to SER
calculation.formation_v2: single-phase equilibrium at the phase's low-T composition, 298.15 K; dfS = S - sum x_i S_i(SER); SER entropies from unary equilibria at 298.15 K
calculation.liquid_mixing: calculate HM/GM of LIQUID minus linear pure-liquid reference

mixing_table.partials: H_i - H_i(pure liquid) from central differences of the integral HM_MIX (h = 1e-4)
mixing_table.reference: pure liquid A and B at T

calculation.order_disorder: composition sets of phases with equivalent sublattices reported in the disordered state are renamed to the disordered lattice phase (e.g. L12_FCC -> FCC_A1)

unit_conversions.formula_unit: value per formula unit = value per mole of atoms x atoms per formula unit

v2.grid: same composition-set-aware grid as the field map
v2.stability_limits: grid limit snapped to an invariant/congruent/melting T within one grid step, otherwise bisection to 0.01 K at a fixed composition

sentences.text: This synthetic document describes the Al–Cu binary system as calculated with pycalphad from the SGTE dataset AlCu-02Mie.tdb; every figure, table and stated value is generated, and the exact values are kept in a separate truth key.
The highest invariant reaction, L → β + (Cu), lies at 1036.7 °C.
The Al–Cu system belongs to the 20 binaries of the ORCHID benchmark, chosen to cover diagram types such as intermetallic rich, peritectic.
The thermodynamic description is the SGTE collection entry [1], which reproduces the assessment of J. Miettinen, Metall. Mater. Trans. A, 33A, 1639-48(2002). [2].
The calculations use pycalphad 0.11.2 at 1 atm.
Pure Al melts at 660.3 °C.
The melting point of Cu reproduced by the dataset is 1084.6 °C.
The eutectic reaction L → β + (Cu) is calculated at 1036.7 °C, with L at x(Cu) = 0.829.
We obtain 1020.6 °C for the peritectic reaction (L + β → γ), where L has x(Cu) = 0.658.
The dataset places a peritectic (L + γ → β) at 993.5 °C; the composition of L is a mole fraction of 0.609.
We obtain 742.1 °C for the peritectic reaction (L + β → ζ), where L has a mole fraction of 0.286.
We obtain 607.9 °C for the eutectic reaction (L → (Al) + ζ), where L has a mole fraction of 0.113.
We obtain 566.9 °C for the eutectoid reaction (β → γ + (Cu)), where β has a mole fraction of 0.762.
The eutectoid reaction ζ → (Al) + β is calculated at 473.9 °C, with ζ at a mole fraction of 0.277.
β melts congruently at 1049.9 °C and x(Cu) = 0.765.
Table 1 compares the calculated temperatures with experimental values from the literature [3–5]; in this synthetic document those values and references are fictitious.
According to Table 2, β remains stable up to 1049.9 °C (congruent melting).
The solubility of Cu in (Al) reaches a mole fraction of 0.054 at 607.9 °C.
At 1450 K the integral mixing enthalpy of the liquid has its minimum, −17.57 kJ/mol, at x(Cu) = 0.600.
The calculated enthalpy of formation of γ at 298.15 K is −20.31 kJ/mol per mole of atoms.
Its heat capacity at room temperature is 24.40 J/(mol K).
For the equiatomic liquid at 1450 K, the Gibbs energy of mixing is −22.08 kJ/mol.
This document is synthetic and exists only to test extraction tools; its truth key lists every boundary, field, invariant, plotted point, table cell and stated value.
